question: Under India's Universal Salt Iodisation programme, iodised salt must contain at least 15 ppm (parts per million) of iodine at the point of consumption.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. India's USI programme mandates ≥15 ppm iodine in salt at point of consumption (≥30 ppm at production). Rock salt and traditional salts do not meet this standard. Cooking in covered vessels helps reduce iodine losses from heat.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The FSSAI/NIDDCP standard requires iodised salt to contain ≥30 ppm at the production level and ≥15 ppm at the point of consumption (household level), accounting for losses during storage and cooking. This ensures adequate iodine delivery to the population.
